I will still do chili on the full 2.0 mu. I have only a small piece of land, so every bag of fertilizer costs me real money, but I do not dare save too much on fertilizer because if the chili sets poorly or the plants stay weak, that loss is bigger than wasting a little fertilizer. I usually start from what worked before and then adjust a bit. For chili here in Quzhou County, with well water available, I will use hybrid seed, because the newer hybrids usually fruit more evenly and stand better, and I have seen that on other people’s fields too. I will prepare the land with rotary tillage because my area is small and that is enough to break the soil and mix fertilizer. On fertilizer, I will not go light. I will put most phosphorus in early, keep nitrogen steady, and give enough potassium because chili needs strong plants and good fruit setting. With well irrigation, I will water after transplanting, then at flowering and fruiting I will not let the field go dry. On pesticide, chili is troublesome if I relax, so I will spray several times through the season, mainly watching aphids, thrips, disease after watering or humid weather, and I will not wait until the field is badly hit. If the weather is normal, I will aim for about 3,000 kg per mu. On my 2 mu, that is a yield level worth chasing.
